transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-06-15
- Start: 17:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Wu (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Head of ML, Silverstream), Priya Nair (Eng Lead), Sam Ortiz (Security Ops)

Auto-summary (auto-gen):
- Silverstream evaluating Redwood for patient-facing summarization and triage features. Interested in fastest path to a working PoC (time-to-first-token) via PLG credits but constrained by PHI/data residency. Leaning towards a hosted quickstart to validate models then private pilot for compliance.

Topics: quickstart credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private, SOC 2 / KMS, VPC peering, latency SLOs, benchmarking plan.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call and then we'll get into where you are and what success looks like.
[00:12] Jordan (Silverstream): Hi all, Jordan here. quick context: we do AI triage and post-discharge summaries, lots of PHI, so security and residency are big for us. We want to move fast tho — see if we can get something demoable in a couple of weeks.
[00:28] Priya: Priya here. engineering wants a low-friction path — ideally time to first token in hours not days. but we also need to know networking and certs up front.
[00:40] Sam: Sam — SecOps. SOC2 yes, SSO, and we use AWS KMS + CloudHSM for keys. We need audit logs.
[00:52] Alex: Great. So two streams — fast PLG path (hosted Redwood API with free credits to validate) vs dedicated/private pilot for compliance. Maya will walk through the quickstart and what changes for dedicated/private.
[01:10] Maya (Redwood SE): quick overview — hosted API gives you immediate keys, SDKs in node/python, streaming, embeddings. we can give credit for a couple thousand requests to validate latency and quality. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and private deploy gives VPC and on-prem options.
[01:35] Jordan: When you say private, do you mean we can run on-prem and have no tokens leave our VPC?
[01:40] Maya: yes, private has a customer-managed control plane option so inference happens in your network. there is still a control-plane handshake depending on the package but we can scope an air-gapped variant if needed.
[01:52] Priya: For time-to-first-token, what's realistic for our team if we try hosted first?
[01:56] Alex: If you go hosted + PLG credits: sign up, API key, drop in a curl call or SDK— you can get a response in under an hour if you have prompts ready. Typical customer flow: create account, get credits, run sample prompts, small integration test.
[02:12] Jordan: That sounds good. our blocker is PHI — can we test with de-identified data on hosted with some contractual terms?
[02:20] Sam: we can't send real PHI to external tenants without specific contractual protections. so we want to know what the contract looks like and whether logs/audit are available.
[02:30] Maya: understood. for hosted test we recommend de-identified data for initial eval. we can also offer a short-term entitlements addendum for logs and retention, but for full PHI support private is the path.
[02:44] Alex: On the question of latency — are you targeting sub-200ms for user-facing calls? what's your typical sequence length?
[02:50] Jordan: For triage we aim for <500ms median, p95 under 1.5s. sequences are short — prompts around 300 tokens.
[03:02] Maya: hosted can often meet that depending on model choice; dedicated with pinned capacity will be more predictable for p95. private gives same runtime but added network hop if peered.
[03:18] Priya: Walk me through the pilot staging — if we do hosted quickstart then move to private pilot, what's the handoff look like?
[03:25] Maya: We'll capture your eval prompts and metrics, then provide a rollout plan. You can pin model version. configs — batching and cache — will transfer to private. there is work to set up VPC peering / SAML and KMS integration. plan on 2-4 weeks for a basic private pilot once infra is ready.
[03:45] Jordan: What about cost — we need estimates. we have about 500K tokens/day projected for month 1 of pilot.
[03:52] Alex: we'll do a cost projection based on model choice. quick rule: hosted per-token pricing vs dedicated reserved capacity which amortizes GPU costs — we'll send an estimate.
[04:05] Sam: Security specifics — do you support customer-managed keys? and are audit logs accessible?
[04:12] Maya: yes, for private we support customer KMS/HSM. for hosted we do provider-managed keys but can enable bring-your-own-key for some tiers. audit logs are available in Redwood Console and can be exported; we can also set up syslog forwarding in dedicated/private.
[04:28] Priya: Any sample benchmark or reference for similar customers in healthcare?
[04:33] Alex: we have anonymized benchmark spreadsheets and a case brief — I'll share links. note: names and exact numbers sanitized.
[04:40] Jordan: awesome. also curious about fallback strategies — if your primary model is unavailable, do you have automatic fallbacks to smaller models?
[04:47] Maya: yes, our smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants and we have canary rollouts. that minimizes downtime, though quality varies.
[04:55] Priya: We also want to run a small accuracy/regression test on a held-out prompt set. how do we pipe evals back into Redwood?
[05:02] Maya: You can push evals into our Optimize tooling; we can set up an eval suite and alert on regressions. during pilot we can instrument token-level quality metrics and link it to rollout policies.
[05:15] Jordan: Ok. Logistics question — if we start with hosted quickstart using de-id data, how long before we can have something demoable to product director?
[05:23] Alex: If you're quick, 48–72 hours to a prototype demo: sign-up, run sample prompts, wire up a webhook or tiny front-end.
[05:30] Priya: any blockers we should know — SDK versions, language support? we primarily use Python and Node.
[05:36] Maya: full support for both. common gotcha: CORS for browser patterns and streaming handshake. we'll include a screenshot and snippet.
[05:45] Jordan: about pilot SOW — will you include an expected token burn and support hours?
[05:50] Alex: yes, pilot SOW includes support SLAs, a burn estimate, and a defined success criteria (latency, accuracy on eval set, integration tests).
[05:58] Sam: Are there any compliance packages or third-party audits?
[06:02] Maya: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and ISO attestations; we can provide certs and a security questionnaire. for specialized HIPAA/BAA requests we have enterprise contracts for private deployments.
[06:15] Jordan: Good. can you also show what the Console looks like for token-level breakdown?
[06:20] Alex: yes I'll share screenshots and a live demo recording.
[06:25] Speaker 2 (mumbled): uh-huh
[06:30] Priya: If we want to test latency at scale, can we run a small spike test on hosted or do we need dedicated?
[06:36] Maya: Hosted can handle a small spike, but for consistent high qps we recommend dedicated reserved capacity. for a pilot-scale spike it's fine to do hosted with us coordinating throttling and routing.
[06:50] Jordan: We also have a security checklist — can you walk through network needs?
[06:54] Maya: VPC peering, egress rules for control-plane (if not air-gapped), optional private link. We'll need IP ranges, peering windows, and cert fingerprints.
[07:08] Sam: For logs retention and SIEM forwarding — do you have built-in integrations?
[07:12] Maya: Yes, we can export logs to S3 or forward to Splunk/Datadog. retention policies can be configured.
[07:20] Alex: Recap so far: 1) Silverstream wants fast PoC (48–72h demo) but cannot put PHI on hosted without contract. 2) Suggested path: Hosted quickstart with de-identified data -> validate latency/quality -> plan private pilot with KMS & VPC peering for PHI. 3) We'll send pricing and SOW options.
[07:40] Jordan: That matches. one other question — do you do model quantization or recommended smaller variants for cost savings?
[07:46] Maya: Yes, Redwood Optimize recommends quantization and model variants. We can propose a quantized variant that reduces tokens/sec cost and often keeps quality.
[07:55] Priya: What's the typical turnaround for dedicated capacity once we decide?
[07:59] Maya: For standard configs 2–3 weeks provisioning; for private on-prem ~3–6 weeks depending on infra.
[08:10] Jordan: Ok. let's talk internal stakeholders — timeline: board wants a pilot by end of July. is that realistic?
[08:16] Alex: Yes — hosted quickstart now + private pilot kickoff mid-July is achievable if security approval and infra windows line up.
[08:24] Priya: We'll need a meeting with our infra and security — Sam will coordinate.
[08:28] Sam: I'll send available peering windows and compliance checklist after this call.
[08:34] Alex: Great. I'll follow up with the pricing sheet, quickstart links, and a sample SOW. Maya will send the runbook and SDK snippets.
[08:42] Jordan: Thanks. would be great to have an example of a healthcare customer flow too.
[08:46] Alex: I'll include an anonymized brief.
[08:48] Maya: Also attaching a short recording that shows Console flows and token-level filters.
[08:55] (brief crosstalk)
[09:00] Alex: Any other questions?
[09:03] Priya: none from me.
[09:05] Jordan: No.
[09:07] Sam: All good.
[09:10] Alex: Ok closing notes: We'll aim to have materials to you by Friday (2027-06-18). Pilot milestones: hosted quickstart (de-id) — demo by Tuesday; private pilot planning — kickoff mid-July.
[09:28] Jordan: Sounds good, thank you both.

End of transcript.
